review_note: The finite-formula reflection principle retains an initial set M₀ and gives a reflecting rank-initial segment V_α with α limit. Original pinned theorem statement checked from Stage A excerpt; no raw proof or remark opened. Preliminary review only.
statement:
Suppose given $\phi_1(x_1, \ldots, x_n), \ldots, \phi_m(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$
a {\bf finite} collection of
formulas of set theory. Let $M_0$ be a set.
There exists a set $M$ such that
$M_0 \subset M$ and
$\forall x_1, \ldots, x_n \in M$, we have
$$
\forall i = 1, \ldots, m, \ \phi_i^{M}(x_1, \ldots, x_n)
\Leftrightarrow
\forall i = 1, \ldots, m, \ \phi_i(x_1, \ldots, x_n).
$$
In fact we may take $M = V_\alpha$ for some limit ordinal $\alpha$.
For a set $M$, $\phi^M$ denotes the formula obtained from $\phi$ by restricting every bound quantifier to range over $M$ (the free variables are among the displayed $x_i$).

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-reflection-principle}
Suppose given $\phi_1(x_1, \ldots, x_n), \ldots, \phi_m(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$
a {\bf finite} collection of
formulas of set theory. Let $M_0$ be a set.
There exists a set $M$ such that
$M_0 \subset M$ and
$\forall x_1, \ldots, x_n \in M$, we have
$$
\forall i = 1, \ldots, m, \ \phi_i^{M}(x_1, \ldots, x_n)
\Leftrightarrow
\forall i = 1, \ldots, m, \ \phi_i(x_1, \ldots, x_n).
$$
In fact we may take $M = V_\alpha$ for some limit ordinal $\alpha$.
